stories.headline: South Korea and Mongolia advance trade pact and critical minerals cooperation South Korean Trade Minister Yeo Han-koo met with Mongolia's Minister of Economy and Development Jadambyn Enkhbayar in the Mongolian capital of Ulaanba
stories.summary: South Korea and Mongolia have agreed to accelerate negotiations on a comprehensive economic partnership agreement (CEPA) to deepen trade ties. The two countries launched CEPA negotiations in 2023 and have held four rounds of talks until November 2024. Recently, South Korean Trade Minister Yeo Han-koo met with Mongolia's Minister of Economy and Development Jadambyn Enkhbayar in Ulaanbaatar to discuss the pact. Mongolia is rich in minerals vital for cutting-edge technologies, and South Korea is seeking to secure a stable supply of these critical minerals. The countries have also launched a vice ministerial-level strategic dialogue to expand cooperation in critical minerals and supply chains. Additionally, South Korea has opened a rare metals cooperation center in Mongolia to help the country strengthen its industrial value chain. The accelerated negotiations aim to finalize the CEPA and enhance bilateral trade cooperation.

stories.headline: Finland and Sweden join major Asia Finland and Sweden will take part in Exercise Pitch Black 2026, one of the largest multinational air force exercises in the Asia-Pacific region
stories.summary: Finland and Sweden will participate in Exercise Pitch Black 2026, a major multinational air force exercise in the Asia-Pacific region. The exercise, conducted by the Royal Australian Air Force, will take place from July 20 to August 7, 2026. It will be held across one of the largest military training areas, featuring demonstration flights of participating countries' combat aircraft. Community events, including a flying display at Mindil Beach in Darwin, are scheduled for July 18 and 20. An "open day" will also be held, allowing local residents to view the aircraft and meet the participants. Exercise Pitch Black 2026 is the Royal Australian Air Force's largest international air exercise, bringing together multiple countries for a period of intensive training and cooperation. The exercise aims to enhance interoperability and strengthen relationships among participating nations.

stories.headline: Steenhuisen could be axed as agriculture minister as early as this week
stories.summary: Agriculture Minister John Steenhuisen may be removed from his position as early as this week due to a cabinet reshuffle. DA leader Geordin Hill-Lewis has requested that President Cyril Ramaphosa replace Steenhuisen with Willie Aucamp as Minister of Agriculture. Steenhuisen, the former DA leader, is expected to be reassigned as Deputy Minister of the Department of Trade, Industry and Competition. The move is part of a broader reshuffle of the DA's Government of National Unity team. The decision is reportedly set to be announced by President Ramaphosa later this week, pending confirmation. Steenhuisen's removal and reassignment are seen as a significant change within the party's leadership structure. The exact timing and details of the reshuffle are expected to be confirmed in the coming days.

stories.headline: How one woman's farm is a model for small Environmental science and conservation news
stories.summary: Diana Sitima's farm in Malawi's Chiradzulu district serves as a model for small-scale environmental science and conservation. Unlike neighboring farmers who primarily grow and sell maize, Sitima's farm showcases a successful combination of agroecology and secure land ownership. This approach has enabled her to create a thriving commercial enterprise. Sitima's story is not isolated, as other farmers like Gorrety have also found success through similar initiatives. Gorrety's journey began with a Child Sponsorship programme and sparked a passion for farming and environmental conservation. These examples demonstrate the potential for small-scale farming to contribute to environmental conservation and economic growth in Malawi and other regions. By adopting agroecological practices and securing land ownership, farmers can create sustainable and profitable businesses.

stories.headline: Elon Musk's xAI launches faster Grok Imagine Video 1.5 with improved audio and physics
stories.summary: xAI, founded by Elon Musk, has launched Grok Imagine Video 1.5, an upgraded image-to-video model with native synchronized audio, sharper physics, and faster generation times. The new model boasts improved motion, physics, and audio, making it the company's strongest model yet. Grok Imagine Video 1.5 has already gained significant attention, accumulating over 268,000 views and topping the Image-to-Video Arena leaderboard. The release highlights the intensifying competition in AI video generation among major players like OpenAI and Google. With its enhanced features and faster speeds, Grok Imagine Video 1.5 is being used to generate a wide range of content, from cinematic clips to creative experiments. The company has made the model available, providing users with a powerful tool for generating high-quality videos.

stories.headline: Microsoft AntiSSRF library is an open-source tool that validates URLs to block server-side request forgery in .NET and Node.js apps
stories.summary: Microsoft has released an open-source AntiSSRF library to combat Server-Side Request Forgery (SSRF) vulnerabilities in web applications. The library validates URLs to block SSRF attacks, supporting both .NET and Node.js apps. It is available under the MIT license, making it easily accessible for developers. SSRF vulnerabilities allow malicious web apps to influence interactions between a client browser and a web app, posing a significant security risk. The AntiSSRF library provides robust URL validation to mitigate this risk, offering a simple and effective solution for developers to protect their web applications. By integrating this library into their apps, developers can help prevent SSRF attacks and ensure a more secure user experience. The library is designed as a drop-in solution, making it easy to implement and use.

stories.headline: Innatera hooks up with Cyran for AI-at-the-edge
stories.summary: Innatera and CYRAN AI have announced an expanded partnership to advance neuromorphic edge artificial intelligence for wearables and intelligent devices. The collaboration aims to develop ultra-low-power gesture and interaction capabilities for next-generation human-machine interfaces. Innatera's spiking neural processor will be utilized to enable low-power AI for edge devices, wearables, and embedded machine learning. The partnership builds on previous demonstrations of their joint solutions, including compact electromyography (EMG) and advanced gesture recognition capabilities. Innatera has also selected Synopsys simulation tools to help scale its brain-inspired processors. The expanded partnership will focus on developing innovative AI solutions for gesture, security, and machine health applications in wearable and intelligent devices.

stories.headline: GIGABYTE AORUS GeForce RTX 5090 INFINITY Priced at 393K in the Philippines
stories.summary: GIGABYTE's AORUS GeForce RTX 5090 INFINITY is now available in the Philippines through DataBlitz, priced at 393,000 Philippine pesos. The graphics card features a WINDFORCE Hyperburst cooling system and is built on NVIDIA's Blackwell architecture. It is designed for high-end gaming, AI workloads, and content creation, making it suitable for professional 3D artists, video editors, and enthusiasts. The AORUS GeForce RTX 5090 INFINITY supports the latest DLSS 4 technology, which brings new Multi Frame Generation and enhanced Ray Reconstruction and Super Resolution. It is powered by GeForce RTX 50 Series GPUs and fifth-generation Tensor Cores, and is backed by an NVIDIA AI supercomputer in the cloud that constantly improves PC gaming capabilities. The card has 32GB of memory and is designed to meet the demands of ultra-high-end local rendering and 8K gaming.

stories.headline: Kylian Mbappe has World Cup history in sights after breaking France scoring record
stories.summary: Kylian Mbappe scored twice in France's 3-1 win over Senegal, breaking France's scoring record and moving closer to Lionel Messi's World Cup goal tally. Mbappe now has 42 goals in 44 games for France and is level with Gerd Mueller in the all-time list. He is behind only Ronaldo and Miroslav Klose in the World Cup career scoring charts, with 15 and 16 goals respectively. With his two goals, Mbappe overtook Pele's mark of 12 World Cup goals and surpassed his former teammate Lionel Messi. The win was part of France's Group I match, and Mbappe's performance has put him in contention to become the tournament's highest ever scorer. He will look to continue his stellar performance to take the record. Mbappe's goals have positioned him as a strong contender for the top scorer title.

stories.headline: Norway 4-1 Iraq: Haaland scores brace on World Cup 2026 debut - as it happened
stories.summary: Erling Haaland scored a hat-trick on his World Cup debut as Norway defeated Iraq 4-1. The match, played at Boston Stadium, marked Norway's first World Cup appearance in 28 years. Haaland's goals helped his team take control of the game, with Leo Østigård also contributing to the score. Iraq put up a spirited display but ultimately fell short against Norway's potent offense. The win is a significant start for Norway in their World Cup campaign, with Haaland's performance drawing praise from teammates, including Sander Berge, who described him as "an animal." The hat-trick brings Haaland's goal tally to 16 goals and 2 assists in 8 matches. Norway's dominant display sets a strong tone for their continued participation in the tournament.

stories.headline: World Cup 2026: Why Cristiano Ronaldo may need the tournament of his life to lift Portugal
stories.summary: Cristiano Ronaldo is set to play in his sixth World Cup as part of Portugal's squad for the 2026 tournament. Despite being an iconic player, there are concerns that he may be an anchor on the team's chances of winning. Portugal coach Roberto Martinez has dismissed these concerns, pointing to Ronaldo's impressive goal-scoring record of 25 goals in his past 31 games for the national team. Martinez has referred to Ronaldo as an "iconic player in global football" ahead of Portugal's Group K clash with the Democratic Republic of the Congo. Ronaldo's participation in the World Cup has brought attention to his potential impact on the team's performance, with some suggesting he may need to have the tournament of his life to help Portugal lift the trophy. Ronaldo will captain the team in the upcoming tournament.

stories.headline: Tab Baldwin, other Ateneo coaches summoned anew by PNP-CIDG
stories.summary: The Philippine National Police-Criminal Investigation and Detection Group (PNP-CIDG) has issued another subpoena to former Ateneo men's basketball head coach Tab Baldwin and other members of the coaching staff. This comes after Baldwin failed to appear in a previous subpoena. The PNP-CIDG is investigating an incident involving Ateneo Blue Eagles players. Baldwin has been asked to submit aerial drone footage from the Aurora, related to the investigation. The new subpoena requires Baldwin and other coaches to appear before the PNP-CIDG to shed light on the incident. The exact nature of the incident and the investigation's focus remain unclear, but the PNP-CIDG is pushing for the coaches' cooperation to move the investigation forward. Baldwin's previous no-show has prompted the issuance of another subpoena, emphasizing the importance of their testimony in the case.

stories.headline: Telegram Moves Delhi High Court Against Centre's Temporary Ban On Platform Over NEET Exam Leak Concerns
stories.summary: Indian authorities have temporarily banned the messaging app Telegram due to concerns over the potential leak of the National Eligibility cum Entrance Test (NEET) exam. The ban aims to prevent organised cheating rackets and the spread of fake information. In response, Telegram has moved the Delhi High Court, challenging the Centre's temporary ban on its platform. The plea is set to be heard by the court. The NEET exam has been marred by a string of leaked papers, prompting the testing body to take measures to prevent cheating. The ban on Telegram is intended to prevent the spread of leaked exam content and tackle cheating rackets ahead of the NEET re-test. The Delhi High Court will hear Telegram's plea against the ban.

stories.headline: T. Veena, daughter of ex-Kerala CM Pinarayi Vijayan, appears before ED for questioning in CMRL pay-off case
stories.summary: T. Veena, daughter of former Kerala Chief Minister Pinarayi Vijayan, appeared before the Enforcement Directorate (ED) in Kochi for questioning in connection with the CMRL monthly payoff case. The case allegedly involves payments amounting to a significant amount. The ED had summoned Veena to appear at its zonal office on June 12, but she appeared on June 17. Security at the ED office was beefed up ahead of her questioning due to previous violent incidents during raids at her father's residence on May 27. Veena's now-defunct IT firm and mining company CMRL are involved in the money laundering case. She is being questioned by ED officials in connection with the case, which is currently under investigation. The questioning is part of the ED's probe into the alleged payoff case and Veena's involvement in it.

stories.headline: Petrol bombs hurled at RSS office in Jharkhand days after stone-pelting on Mohan Bhagwat's train; CCTV footage emerges
stories.summary: Petrol bombs were hurled at an RSS office in Ranchi, Jharkhand, in the early hours of Wednesday. The incident occurred just days after stone-pelting on RSS chief Mohan Bhagwat's train. CCTV footage has emerged, showing two youths throwing petrol bombs at the office. Opposition leader Babulal Marandi has been mentioned in relation to the incident. The attack took place late at night on Tuesday, with the CCTV visuals capturing the moment the petrol bombs were hurled. The incident has been reported by various news outlets, with footage and updates being shared on social media. An investigation into the attack is likely to be underway, with authorities reviewing the CCTV footage to identify the perpetrators. The incident has raised concerns about the safety and security of RSS offices and personnel.

stories.headline: Attackers who slapped Abhijeet Dipke at CJP protest in Jaipur garlanded after release | Video
stories.summary: Abhijeet Dipke, founder of CJP, was slapped and assaulted during a protest in Jaipur. The incident occurred while he was being carried on the shoulders of supporters, with miscreants in the crowd pulling at his scarf and attempting to pull him down. The attackers, alleged to be from the RSS, were later released and given a hero's welcome, with supporters garlanding them. Dipke stated that he will not be intimidated and will continue to raise his voice, saying physical attacks are a sign of fear and cowardice. The CJP has vowed to continue holding peaceful protests, undeterred by the assault. Videos of the incident have gone viral on social media, sparking widespread reaction. Dipke has taken to social media to condemn the attack and reaffirm his commitment to peaceful protest.

stories.headline: US and Europe discuss ‘trusted partner’ AI pact after Anthropic export restrictions
stories.summary: The US and Europe are discussing a "trusted partner" scheme for access to advanced AI models, following US export restrictions on Anthropic. The US government ordered Anthropic to suspend access to its most advanced models, including Fable 5 and Mythos 5, for foreign users. In response, Anthropic disabled access to these models for all users to comply with the directive. G7 leaders have discussed a plan to grant select "trusted partners" access to these models. The move has sparked calls for Europe to accelerate development of its own cutting-edge AI models, amid concerns over reliance on US technology. The export controls have raised questions about global access to advanced AI and the need for international cooperation on AI development and regulation. Talks are ongoing to establish a framework for trusted partners to access restricted AI models.

stories.summary: Google is replacing news headlines in its search results with AI-generated ones. This change is part of the company's efforts to improve its search results. The AI-generated headlines are intended to provide more accurate and concise summaries of news articles. The move has been observed in recent search results, where traditional headlines from news sources are being replaced by AI-generated alternatives. This development has sparked interest and discussion online, with some users noticing the change and sharing their observations. The use of AI-generated headlines raises questions about the role of artificial intelligence in shaping the way people consume news and information online. Google's decision to introduce AI-generated headlines is a significant development in the evolving landscape of online news consumption.

stories.headline: Shikha Mukerjee | Congress’ Fading Grandeur and Momentum of Inertia Opposition in the Lok Sabha, the Congress, has been consistent in facing off against the BJP
stories.summary: The Congress party, led by the Opposition in the Lok Sabha, has consistently faced off against the BJP. Political analyst Shikha Mukerjee notes a significant anti-incumbency sentiment against Mamata Banerjee in West Bengal. Recently, Mukerjee suggested that the TMC should take to the streets after deleted voters were denied welfare schemes in the state. The BJP, led by Chief Minister Suvendu Adhikari, has been gaining momentum in West Bengal. Adhikari addressed supporters during the BJP government's swearing-in ceremony at Brigade Parade Grounds in Kolkata. Mukerjee, a senior journalist based in Kolkata, has been providing analysis on the political landscape in West Bengal, highlighting the challenges faced by the TMC and the Congress party in the state. Her comments come amid ongoing political developments in the region.

stories.headline: Congress Faces Internal Power Struggle as Party Leaders Clash Over Election Strategy
stories.summary: Congress is experiencing an internal power struggle as party leaders clash over election strategy. The recent passage of a budget outline on a party-line vote highlighted the GOP's difficulties, with a surge of money for tough immigration enforcement being a point of contention. An internal House Republican dispute over cryptocurrency legislation led to a delayed process vote, showcasing the party's divisions. Meanwhile, President Donald Trump is facing growing opposition within his own party, with Republican lawmakers becoming more willing to break ranks with him. This internal conflict is expected to intensify as the midterm elections approach, with the first major primary day putting pressure on lawmakers to take a stand. The clash between Trump's governance style and Republicans' political survival instincts is driving the party's internal struggles.

stories.headline: BJP Launches Scathing Attack on Congress Over Economic Policies and Corruption Allegations
stories.summary: The BJP has launched a scathing attack on the Congress party over its economic policies and corruption allegations. The attack targets the Congress government in Karnataka, accusing them of using the state as a source of funds. The BJP has been consistently criticizing the Congress party, highlighting its alleged compromised mission and compromised story. The party has been sharing stories and evidence on social media, aiming to expose the Congress party's wrongdoings. The attack is part of the BJP's efforts to expand its base and gain an upper hand in the political landscape. The party has been poaching leaders from opposition parties, including the Congress, to strengthen its position. The BJP's criticism of the Congress party is ongoing, with the party consistently accusing them of corruption and mismanagement.

stories.headline: Lok Sabha Witnesses Heated Debate Between Congress and BJP Over Key Legislative Bills
stories.summary: The Lok Sabha witnessed heated debates between Congress and BJP members over key legislative bills during the 2026 Budget Session and Winter Session. The discussions centered around several bills, including the Constitution 31st Amendment Bill 2026, the Delimitation Bill 2026, and the Union Territory Laws Bill 2026. Additionally, the Women's Reservation Bill is set for crucial voting. Tensions escalated with clashes and heated exchanges between members of the two parties, as well as with other parties like the TMC. The debates have been intense, with opposition members raising objections to the bills and the government pushing for their passage. The Lok Sabha has seen disruptions and heated discussions on various occasions, including during the discussion on the Budget 2024. The voting on these key bills is expected to be crucial.

stories.headline: Stock Market Highlights June 17: Sensex gains 347 pts, Nifty closes at 24,085 on easing crude oil prices
stories.summary: Indian equity benchmark indices extended gains for the fourth consecutive session on Wednesday, with the Sensex climbing 347.14 points to 77,155.62 and the Nifty rising 96.55 points to 24,085.70. The gains were supported by easing crude oil prices and positive global cues. Ten of the 16 major sectors advanced, with small-caps and mid-caps increasing by 0.8% and 0.5%, respectively. The Nifty 50 index closed above the 24,000 level for the first time in three weeks. The rally was driven by gains in various sectors, including goods and power stocks. The Sensex and Nifty ended 0.45% and 0.40% higher, respectively, marking their fourth consecutive day of gains. The positive trend was influenced by favorable global market sentiments and declining crude oil prices.

stories.headline: Sensex, Nifty extend gains as US-Iran peace deal cools crude oil prices
stories.summary: Indian shares extended gains for a fourth consecutive session, with the Sensex and Nifty indices rising due to a significant drop in crude oil prices. The decline in oil prices is attributed to easing geopolitical tensions following a preliminary US-Iran peace deal. The Sensex surged over 1,100 points, while the Nifty crossed the 24,000 milestone. The peace agreement has improved risk sentiment, boosting investor optimism and driving the Indian equity benchmarks higher. Crude oil prices have plunged, providing further support to the markets. The Nifty has consistently traded above the 24,000 mark, driven by the positive sentiment surrounding the US-Iran peace framework and lower crude oil prices. The Indian benchmark indices have now advanced for four straight sessions, reflecting the improved market mood.

stories.headline: Stock markets today: Sensex, Nifty extend gains as crude oil prices drop, IT stocks surge
stories.summary: Indian benchmark indices, Sensex and Nifty, extended their rally for the fourth consecutive day, driven by a drop in crude oil prices and strong performance from IT firms. Brent crude slipped to around $78.44 per barrel, easing inflation worries and boosting IT stocks like Infosys, TCS, Tech Mahindra, and HCL Tech. The 30-share BSE Sensex climbed, while Axis Bank and Bajaj Finance lagged. The decline in crude oil prices to three-month lows improved India's inflation outlook, boosting investor optimism. The rally in IT firms also contributed to the gains in the stock market. The Sensex and Nifty have been on an upward trend, with the current rally marking the fourth consecutive day of gains, despite mixed global cues.

stories.headline: Stock Market LIVE: GIFT Nifty signals tepid open; Asia mkts mixed as traders await US Fed decision
stories.summary: Indian markets started the day slowly on Wednesday, with GIFT Nifty futures trading flat, indicating no significant price movement. Asian markets were mixed overnight, with some indexes rising and others falling. The cautious start comes ahead of the US Federal Reserve's decision, which investors are eagerly awaiting for signals on interest rate cuts. The Nifty 50 is expected to follow the trend set by the GIFT Nifty futures. Meanwhile, IT stocks have come under pressure due to uncertainty over the US Fed's rate cut signals. The domestic market is also eyeing India's June manufacturing PMI for further cues. Overall, the market mood is cautious, with investors adopting a wait-and-watch approach ahead of the key events.

stories.headline: Hon Hai Technology Group (Foxconn) Accelerates Global Leadership In AI Factories, Infrastructure At Europe's VivaTech
stories.summary: Hon Hai Technology Group, also known as Foxconn, showcased its end-to-end integration capabilities at VivaTech, accelerating its global leadership in AI factories and sovereign AI infrastructure. The company demonstrated its ability to stand up the world's most advanced, rack-scale AI supercomputer. Foxconn has also collaborated with Schneider Electric to define and scale the next generation of AI data centers. Additionally, the company has partnered with NVIDIA to accelerate AI development, featuring the Vera Rubin NVL72 and humanoid technologies, as well as modular data centers. These initiatives aim to strengthen Foxconn's global competitiveness through innovation in next-generation AI technologies, including AI memory and data center infrastructure. The collaborations and technological advancements position Foxconn as a leader in the AI era, driving development of core technologies and infrastructure.

stories.headline: IR launches Iris for HPE Nonstop, bringing AI-powered observability insights to mission-critical infrastructure
stories.summary: Integrated Research has launched Iris for HPE Nonstop, extending its conversational AI intelligence layer to HPE Nonstop environments. Iris is powered by IR's Prognosis platform and translates complex monitoring data into actionable insights, answering plain language questions. The solution provides AI-powered observability insights to mission-critical infrastructure, offering clients a deeper understanding of their systems. Iris for Nonstop is available now with Prognosis 13.3, for clients using IR Infrastructure and the Prognosis Platform for HPE Nonstop. The natural-language, AI-powered Prognosis Assistant is purpose-built for HPE NonStop, making deep insights instantly accessible. This launch aims to bring AI-powered intelligence directly to the IT function, providing unique context and understanding for each client's environment.

stories.headline: Aer Lingus slashes senior management and Revenue takes on local politics
stories.summary: Aer Lingus has reduced its senior management numbers by 25%. The move is part of an urgent cost-cutting drive, which also includes slashing flights. The airline's decision comes as pilots question expansion plans, potentially impacted by local politicians' actions. Former IAG boss Willie Walsh has expressed concern about the airline's situation. The cost-cutting measures are likely aimed at improving the airline's financial stability. Meanwhile, Revenue is taking on local politics, although details of this involvement are not specified. The developments at Aer Lingus reflect the challenges faced by the airline industry, with companies seeking to adapt to changing circumstances and maintain viability. The reduction in senior management and flights is expected to have significant implications for the airline's operations and future plans.

stories.headline: Virgin Australia urged to refund travellers with COVID
stories.summary: Virgin Australia is reminding customers to use their COVID-era flight credits before June 30, 2026, or risk losing their value. The airline has given travellers until the end of the month to claim and use their credits. Customers with credits from cancelled flights must book and complete their travel by June 30. Virgin Australia is reaching out to customers about $90 million in credits set to expire, while Qantas is holding $358 million in unused credits. Unlike Qantas, which still offers refunds for eligible unused credits, Virgin Australia's credits will become void if not used by the deadline. Customers are being urged to book and complete their travel before the end of June to avoid forfeiting their credits. The airline is contacting customers to remind them to use their credits before they expire.

stories.headline: S. Korea 4th country to forge AI security alliance with OpenAI
stories.summary: South Korea has formed an AI security partnership with OpenAI, becoming the fourth country to do so. The agreement was made under a memorandum of understanding between OpenAI and the Ministry of Science and ICT's AI Safety Institute. This partnership strengthens South Korea's position in the global cooperation network aimed at verifying risks of advanced AI and establishing safety protocols. The deal broadens an October 2025 cooperation agreement between the ministry and OpenAI, extending it into the safety arena. The move is part of South Korea's efforts to prioritize AI investment, with research spending increasing nearly 20% to a record 35.3 trillion won ($25.23 billion) to support flagging growth. The partnership is expected to enhance South Korea's AI safety capabilities and contribute to global efforts in mitigating AI risks.

stories.headline: SpaceX Investor Powerlaw Debuts Amid IPO Race
stories.summary: SpaceX investor Powerlaw has debuted amid a heated IPO race, with the closed-end fund trading above the value of its underlying stakes in SpaceX and OpenAI. This comes as SpaceX is reportedly preparing for a June 2026 IPO, with a potential valuation of $1.75 trillion, fueled by its Starlink subsidiary's 10 million subscribers. The IPO could raise over $30 billion, making it one of the largest in history. Elon Musk has confirmed plans for SpaceX to go public in 2026, with a valuation of $1.5 trillion. The debut of Powerlaw and the anticipated SpaceX IPO have raised questions about valuation, governance, and the future of AI-related IPOs. The IPO race is expected to continue, with several high-profile listings planned for the coming months. SpaceX's IPO is highly anticipated, given its significant growth and valuation.

The partnership is expected to enhance AI safety and security in the country, aligning with its goal of becoming a leading AI nation. This collaboration with OpenAI is a key part of South Korea's strategy to advance its AI capabilities and stay competitive in the global AI landscape.

stories.headline: SpaceX Investor Powerlaw Debuts Amid IPO Race
stories.summary: Powerlaw, a closed-end fund, has announced its stake in SpaceX is valued at approximately $117.0 million, representing 19.37% of its net assets. This makes SpaceX the fund's single largest position. The valuation comes as SpaceX prepares for a potential IPO, with Powerlaw standing to benefit from the private space company's debut. Powerlaw's investment in SpaceX is part of its portfolio, which also includes stakes in other prominent companies such as OpenAI, Databricks, and Perplexity. The fund's exposure to SpaceX has contributed to its recent gains, with Powerlaw's shares jumping in response to the news. The development is part of a broader trend of sector-wide growth, with Powerlaw's announcement highlighting the potential benefits of investing in private companies on the verge of going public.
